payload.claim: When `run_regate` declines (returns 1, writing no row) on a retried adopt, the `why` message is built only from `ledger.regate(task_id)`, which can still return a stale row from an earlier, successful re-gate of the same task. The code never checks `outcome` here, so a decline (e.g. the pull request has since been merged or closed, making `_pull_request_state` raise `_Declined`) is reported as 'its re-gate recorded N new failure(s)' or 'names ..., not the adopted head' using leftover data from a prior attempt, instead of naming the decline. The task's state is still kept correctly (the move is gated on `outcome == 0` a few lines above), but the printed reason an operator reads to decide what to do next can describe a run that never happened. This path is explicitly outside what the tests exercise (the task notes say to give each decline case 'a fresh task that holds no re-gate row'), so no gate or test catches it.
